variant_policy: Count each distinct word-meaning once across the recorded readings. Keep the attribution of additional meanings. A union of readings is a research inventory, not a claim that every commentator accepted every meaning. Qualified uses and unenumerated remainders remain separate.
description: Source-entry-specific interpretation decisions. These settle the listed glosses, not every fine-grained lexical sense or all derivational eligibility. Original source wording remains unchanged.

decisions.decision: Four meanings: requesting, affliction, lordship, and blessing. The commentary treats both citations together. Do not split the word for blessing further.
decisions.eligibility: The commentary distinguishes pada use according to meaning; preserve that condition for generation.

decisions.decision: Two descriptions: instruction and auspicious action. Shasana explains shastra here; the parenthesis is not a third sense.
One qualified action associated with a habitual biter. Preserve the qualification; the snake-biting parenthesis is not an additional independent meaning.

Three meanings in the reading attributed to Kshirasvamin: movement, crookedness, and diminution. The commentary separately records the two-member reading. Retain that provenance rather than inferring the count from the dual ending.
Count one covering description. Madhaviya gives chadana; the concordance gives acchadana for the same entry. There is no separate meaning established merely by the added prefix in the gloss.
Five meanings are separately enumerated, including giving and taking. The final adana is not another occurrence of dana.
Nineteen source-listed meanings. Svamyartha is one member, not svamya plus artha. This resolves segmentation; relationships among the broad senses still belong to lexical review.
The commentary separates begging, non-attainment, and attainment. The source does not treat the whole phrase as a single qualification of begging.
Five members. Vratadesha remains one member; do not split every noun inside the compound.

decisions.anchor: वादित्रग्रहणं नाम वादित्रस्य वाद्यभाण्डस्य वादनार्थं ग्रहणमिति
decisions.decision: Five meanings, not six. The commentary explicitly joins vaditra and grahana: taking up a musical instrument to play it. It also records the dental-n citation as a reading; the identity relationship between the two citations remains open.
One smelling description. Ghrana explains the same action rather than establishing an additional sense.
Keep the unprefixed abhibhava description as one assignment. The commentary illustrates nyunibhava with para-jayate; do not add that prefixed reading as a second unprefixed-base meaning.
One sharpening description, with nishana explaining the relevant action rather than adding a second count.
decisions.eligibility: The commentary calls this entry nitya-sananta. Do not automatically treat a san derivation as creating another base from a simple productive input.

decisions.decision: The heading is a qualified movement description, not censure plus movement. Retain one broad assignment here; the commentary discusses flight and sleep and says sleep is generally ni-prefixed. Separate those readings in prefix-aware lexical work.
decisions.eligibility: Sleep reading is generally ni-prefixed; no automatic new unprefixed sense.

decisions.decision: The cross-reference is explicitly explained as satisfaction. The commentary records the two-entry reading, while disputing the inclusion of sah in this class; preserve the entry and its provenance flag.
decisions.eligibility: The sah entry is disputed among the cited grammatical traditions; select scope before full generation.

decisions.decision: Resolve the reference to vrnoti as varana, choosing. Do not treat the cross-reference phrase as an additional meaning.
Two meanings: hastening movement and harming. Gati-tvarana is a single qualified action here, which explains the dual ending.
Three members in the main reading: affection, cutting, and removal. The commentary also records a shorter alternative reading; do not add that list to this one.
One kindling or intensifying description. Dipana and sandipana do not establish two independent meanings for this entry.
Pad's meaning is explicitly glossed as movement. The entry is headed anga-sad, so the meaning belongs to the specified a-prefixed use.
decisions.eligibility: Requires AN prefix in this source entry; not an unrestricted bare-base input.

decisions.decision: That action points to the nominal meaning sukha: making happy. This is not the same meaning as the adjacent duhkha entry.
decisions.eligibility: Nominal-derived input; avoid recounting the same formation in the noun-to-verb stage.

decisions.decision: That action points to the nominal meaning duhkha: causing distress. The shared shorthand does not make sukha and duhkha the same meaning.
decisions.eligibility: Nominal-derived input; avoid recounting the same formation in the noun-to-verb stage.

decisions.decision: Three meanings: applying colour, elaborating, and describing qualities or praising. The commentary supplies separate examples for the three uses.
decisions.eligibility: Nominal-derived input; coordinate with the noun-to-verb inventory.

decisions.decision: Admit one broad crushing/rubbing meaning from the base-patha entry for prud itself. Do not add a second meaning merely for vimardana/pramardana. The previously inspected mut commentary is not evidence for this citation.
decisions.remaining: Locate commentary on prud to determine whether the second description adds a distinct meaning. The two transcriptions differ (vimardana versus pramardana); the one admitted assignment does not settle that difference.

mardane.reading: Base patha; one broad meaning admitted, second description unresolved.

decisions.decision: Admit sowing, impregnation, and cutting. The commentary explains bija-santana as scattering seed in a field and gives separate pregnancy and hair-cutting examples. Shaving is included in the cutting assignment, not added as another word-meaning here.
decisions.remaining: The pinned inventory also names rubbing and thread-making and combines bija/tantu descriptions. The three inspected commentaries do not locate those additions. Keep them in the original gloss and seek their source; do not claim that this three-meaning subtotal exhausts vap.

bIjasantAne.reading: Main meaning, explained as scattering seed in a field.

garBADAne.reading: Additional use explicitly recorded in the commentary.

Cedane.reading: Additional cutting use, illustrated with hair.

decisions.decision: Five meanings occur in the main vi heading: movement, conception, desire, throwing, and eating. Kshiratarangini explicitly records an alternative ashana reading as pervasion, supplying the sixth meaning. Vevi explicitly refers to vi's meanings; retain the two lexical inputs separately pending identity review. Their shared list does not make them one word.
decisions.eligibility: The vevi entry 02.0072 is described as Vedic-only. The shared review does not apply that restriction to vi 02.0043. The pervasion assignment retains its alternative-reading attribution; do not imply agreement across all witnesses.

gatO.reading: Main vi heading; vevi inherits the list through the explicit cross-reference.

prajanane.reading: Main reading, explained as initial conception.

vyAptO.reading: Alternative reading attributed to some; not inferred from the separate i entry.

cross_reference.decision: Vevi is assigned the meanings of vi. Source XA766 independently records the Vedic-only restriction.

decisions.decision: Four recorded meanings: offering/giving, eating, taking, and satisfying. Adana (taking) appears in alternative readings and is counted once. Adana with short initial a is eating, a different meaning. Prinana is explicitly discussed at the end of the commentary; it is not an unsupported addition. Offering and its explanation as depositing an oblation are one assignment here.

dAne.reading: Main reading, explained as depositing an oblation.

adane.reading: Main reading explicitly explained as eating.

AdAne.reading: Alternative reading: taking; repeated mention is not another count.

prIRane.reading: Additional satisfying use, attributed to the Bhashya and illustrated in the commentary.

decisions.decision: Admit growth, accomplishment, and consideration of someone's fortune. Madhaviya explicitly discusses the latter two beyond the heading's growth meaning. Its droha example uses apa-radh and vi-radh, so that meaning is reserved for the prefix stage rather than counted as another bare-base meaning.
decisions.remaining: The pinned gloss ends in adi and does not enumerate the rest. Further meanings are not assigned a number. Retain the disagreement with Kshiratarangini about the fourth-class use beyond growth for the eligibility stage.
decisions.eligibility: Droha is evidenced through apa-/vi-prefixed uses here. Madhaviya and Kshiratarangini differ on class restrictions; a union of documented meanings is not unrestricted permission to generate every class form.

dEvaparyAlocane.reading: Additional unprefixed use discussed in Madhaviya.

decisions.decision: Three documented candidate meanings, not four: affection, protection, and living. Priti is shared by the two readings and counts once. The alternative calana is explicitly explained as jivana; those two descriptions count once, not as movement plus living. The two readings retain their attribution.
decisions.eligibility: The commentary records Vedic-only treatment of sprnoti; retain that restriction for the initial laukika run.

prItO.reading: Shared by the main and alternative pairs; counted once.

jIvane.reading: Alternative pair's second member, explained as living by Svamin.

decisions.decision: Three documented candidate meanings: affection, seeing, and attending/serving. The shared priti contributes once; darshana and sevana retain their separate main/alternative-reading provenance. The source presents them as different descriptions and does not equate them. Finer contextual sense review remains separate from this list-level count.

prItO.reading: Shared by both pairs; counted once.

open_reviews.decision: The commentary records general action and many meanings as explanations of the unspecified entry. Neither supplies a list of distinct lexical meanings. Keep the entry outside the numerical subtotal, with a blank count rather than zero.

The commentary refers back to kage and distinguishes this van entry from other same-looking entries. It supplies no finite list of meanings. Keep this entry outside the numerical subtotal; do not import the meanings of another van merely from shared spelling.

identity_decisions.decision: The commentary explicitly calls the first jval entry a repetition for mit status. Count the shared shining meaning once, while retaining both source records and their grammatical information.
The later gadi entry refers back to the same entry in the earlier dental section. Count this repeated entry-and-meaning once, retaining both locators.
